text:
incident-bot: Pager — P1: elevated 5xx rate on /v1/generate (prod-us-east). Triggered at 2026-03-12T14:00:00Z. Auto-escalation sent to #incidents and on-call.
priya_sre: seeing the spike on grafana. Canaries show errors jumping right after the 14:00 deploy. tagging @dan_eng oncall.
dan_eng: on it. which release?
carol_prod: release id: r-2026-03-12-14:00 (canary rollout). Canary hosts failing health checks, full prod still has some traffic.
priya_sre: automation attempted an automated rollback but it returned 500 from deploy API — looks like the deploy-controller hit rate limits. I tried to requeue and it errored.
dan_eng: ack. I'll try manual rollback and feature flag kill-switch in parallel.
ryan_pm: heads-up — several customers reported degraded responses (support queue rising). @jen_support is triaging.
jen_support: a couple of paying customers (acct: brightshop, acct: eduplan) reported timeouts and >50% request failures. logging their request ids.
dan_eng: first step: flip the feature flag that was toggled for the canary (feature_xyz). If that doesn't stabilize, we do manual deployment rollback. I'm on terminal.
priya_sre: //priya on prod net
priya_sre: recommend setting incident channel to urgent and initiating customer impact template.
dan_eng: running flag disable now:
```
# disable feature flag via internal tool
redwood-ff toggle --env prod --feature feature_xyz --off --reason "canary failures 14:00"
```
deploy-bot: feature flag feature_xyz turned OFF in prod by dan_eng at 2026-03-12T14:02:13Z.
carol_prod: metrics: error-rate edge -> dropped from 13% to 4% within 45s of flag flip on canaries. but some older sessions still failing.
priya_sre: good signal. keep monitoring. however traffic to new replicas still exists; we should roll back the canary group to previous revision to avoid lingering bad nodes.
dan_eng: starting manual rollback for deployment/redwood-api -n prod (canary subset). Command:
```
kubectl -n prod rollout undo deployment/redwood-api --to-revision=142
kubectl -n prod get pods -l role=canary -o wide
```
dan_eng: kube accepted rollback, creating old pods. watching events.
priya_sre: checking logs: recent crash loops originated from model-chunk loader hitting OOM while warming kv-cache under new change. that fits the failure pattern.
jen_support: I'm updating affected customers: telling them we rolled back canary and disabled suspect feature, will confirm when errors normalize.
carol_prod: canary pod counts back to stable revision. health checks passing on all restarted pods.
priya_sre: validating traffic split — router still sending small percent to canary until host drain completes. initiating immediate traffic shift to stable:
```
redwood-router update-split --service api --prod --canary-weight 0
```
dan_eng: confirmed traffic split now 100% stable.
priya_sre: run quick smoke tests:
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.prod.redwood/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"smoke test"}' | jq .status
```
dan_eng: smoke returned OK for 10 sequential requests, latency normal.
deploy-bot: automated rollback task originally failed at 14:01:12Z due to deploy-controller rate limit. Manual rollback succeeded at 14:06:45Z.
carol_prod: observed error-rate back to baseline (<1%) across all regions within ~3m of rollback + flag-off.
jen_support: forwarded confirmations to customers; they acknowledge.
ryan_pm: good. we should keep the incident open until postmortem and RCA. Can we capture exact change that introduced OOM?
priya_sre: yes — reproducing locally against r-2026-03-12-14:00. crash trace points to kv-cache prefetch change in model-loader v2. Dan, can you file a revert/patch PR?
dan_eng: filing PR now: PR #3149 "revert kv-cache prefetch change for stability". Linking to incident.
jen_support: customers asked for ETA on fix — I'll say "hotfix targeted within 24 hours after RCA".
priya_sre: follow-up items for postmortem: 1) why automated rollback failed (deploy-controller rate limit) 2) improve auto-rollback retry/backoff 3) add circuit-breaker in model-loader for OOM protection 4) test feature flag gating earlier in canary steps.
carol_prod: also add a playbook step: if auto-rollback fails, system should automatically reduce LB weight for canary to 0 before manual intervention.
dan_eng: agreed. I'm adding checklist to the PR for validation steps and an additional e2e smoke in deploy pipeline.
priya_sre: status summary for the channel: manual rollback succeeded, feature flag disabled, customers notified, errors returned to baseline. Keeping incident open for RCA & follow-ups.
jen_support: closing customer-facing tickets as "mitigated".
incident-bot: Incident P1 annotated: mitigated at 2026-03-12T14:09:00Z; next step: postmortem due in 48h and assignment to dan_eng and priya_sre for RCA.
ryan_pm: thanks all. Will schedule a short wartime retro 1hr after this thread closes.
priya_sre: adding timeline and logs to incident doc now (https://internal.redwood/incidents/1768450000).
carol_prod: final check: I'll re-run canary perf tests in staging with memory safety flags before we re-enable feature_xyz.
jen_support: leaving notes for CS to contact affected customers when fix deploys.
dan_eng: thanks everyone, switching to follow-up mode."
